# RelaySwarm

> Peer-assisted HLS video delivery needs rendezvous infrastructure, and the
> usual answer is a dedicated, application-specific tracker. RelaySwarm is a
> proof of concept that rendezvouses peers over the same Nostr relays a
> live-stream event already lists (NIP-53), so peer discovery reuses
> redundant, stream-selected infrastructure instead of a project-operated
> service.

RelaySwarm is for people building or evaluating peer-assisted delivery for
Nostr live-streaming clients (zap.stream and similar). It proves the claim
end to end over two paths: a browser path (WebRTC, signalled over Nostr
relays) and a native path for installed Node applications (HyperDHT and
Noise, no STUN or TURN). Both verify transferred data by SHA-256 before
trusting it. This is a proof of concept: multi-peer swarm scheduling, an
hls.js loader plugin and a NIP draft are deliberately out of scope for the
code here (see the README's "Deliberately out of scope" section).

## Getting Started

There is no npm release yet; use a git dependency pinned at a commit, or run
the proofs of concept directly from a checkout:

```bash
npm ci
npm test                   # end-to-end: PoC + fan-out, against live Nostr relays
npm run poc                # two-peer WebRTC PoC
npm run poc:native         # two-peer native HyperDHT PoC
```

`npm test` needs Node 22+ and an internet connection: it signs, transfers and
verifies against real public relays, and exits non-zero on a failed
verification.

## Key Concepts

- **Presence and signal events.** A seeder announces presence as an
  ephemeral, swarm-tagged Nostr event; peers exchange WebRTC SDP as
  ephemeral, `p`-tagged signal events over the same relays.
- **Hash-verified transfer.** Every received object is checked against a
  SHA-256 digest before use; a bad seeder controls both bytes and hash in
  the current PoC, so this detects corruption, not a malicious peer.
- **Two independent transports.** The browser path uses WebRTC data
  channels; the native path uses HyperDHT with NIP-44-encrypted dial
  authorisation, for installed Node applications that cannot open a
  browser's RTCPeerConnection.
- **Shadow mode.** `hls-swarm.mjs` races the swarm against the origin
  inside a real hls.js player without changing what the viewer sees, so
  peer-delivery numbers can be collected safely.
- **Risk-tiered participation.** A viewer can run origin-only, with no
  swarm subscription or event publication, and never appear in the swarm.

## API Surface

From `relayswarm` (`src/relay-session.mjs`):
- `RelaySwarmSession`, `RelayPool` - swarm membership, presence and
  signalling over a set of Nostr relays.
- `validTicket(ticket)` - validates an admission ticket.
- `KIND_PRESENCE`, `KIND_SIGNAL`, `SWARM_TAG` - the Nostr event kinds and
  tag name the protocol uses.

From `relayswarm/hls-swarm` (`src/browser/hls-swarm.mjs`):
- `createHlsSwarm(options)` - attaches shadow-mode peer assist to an
  hls.js player; see [`INTEGRATION.md`](INTEGRATION.md) for the full
  host-page contract, options and kill switch.
- `rotationCandidate(links, options, at)`, `retryAfterFor(links, options,
  lastEvictionAt, at)` - peer link rotation and backoff.

Native path (not published as package exports; imported from source):
- `src/native-dht-transport.mjs`'s `NativeDhtTransport` and
  `src/native-journey.mjs`'s `runNativeJourney` drive the HyperDHT transfer;
  see [`docs/NATIVE-TRANSPORT.md`](docs/NATIVE-TRANSPORT.md) for the
  protocol and security boundary.
- `src/object-transfer.mjs` frames, hashes and verifies transferred objects.
